sections.skill: Compute contribution per order and compare it with acquisition cost

questions.prompt: Price 40; product 15, packaging 2, shipping 8, fees 1.50. What is the contribution per order?
questions.intro: UNIT ECONOMICS looks at whether one sale (or one customer) makes money. For one order: price minus all costs that come with that order (product, packaging, shipping, payment fees, and any discount) gives the CONTRIBUTION per order. If you pay to get customers, compare CUSTOMER ACQUISITION COST (CAC: marketing spend / new customers) with how much contribution a customer brings over time. Growing a business with negative unit economics grows the losses.

sections.skill: A lemonade stand that pays people to stop by

questions.prompt: The 1 dollar paid per new customer is like what?

choices.text: The price per cup of lemonade

questions.intro: Imagine a lemonade stand earning 50 cents of profit per cup but paying a friend 1 dollar for every new customer he brings. If each customer buys only one cup, the stand loses 50 cents per customer, and the busier it gets, the more it loses. If customers come back for 3 cups, the stand earns 3 x 0.50 = 1.50 per customer before the referral cost, so 1.50 - 1 = 0.50 is left after paying the friend, and the deal works.

questions.prompt: With one cup per customer, what happens?

choices.text: It earns 50 cents for each new customer
The stand loses 50 cents per customer

questions.correct_answer: The stand loses 50 cents per customer
